# Tempolight

> Tempolight is free, open-source (MIT) music-reactive lighting for WLED and smart lights: an alternative to LedFx. It finds the beat, the bars, the build-ups and the drops, picks one look per song, and plays it across every light in a room as one canvas. Plain JavaScript for Node.js 20+ with zero dependencies; runs on Windows, macOS, Linux, a Raspberry Pi, in Docker or as a Home Assistant add-on, and is used from a browser or as a phone app (PWA).

Key facts:

- Lights: WLED (DDP, E1.31, Art-Net), any E1.31/Art-Net receiver, DMX fixtures through an Art-Net or sACN node, Philips Hue (basic and Entertainment), Nanoleaf, Govee (beta), LIFX, WiZ, TP-Link Kasa, Yeelight, Twinkly, OpenRGB, and phones as lights.
- Music in: songs analysed before they play, live listening (this computer's sound, a microphone, a sound card on a Raspberry Pi), Sync with Spotify, now playing from music apps, song memory, a music folder analysed ahead, Pioneer Pro DJ Link, Ableton Link, MIDI clock, OSC.
- Smart home and creators: Home Assistant (MQTT discovery and an add-on), Apple Home (a HomeKit bridge, so Siri works), OBS, Stream Deck, Twitch, Discord, CS2 and Dota 2 game events.
- Web UI and API on port 8080 by default (http://localhost:8080, or http://tempolight.local on the Raspberry Pi image). Settings are kept in ~/.tempolight.
- Start it: `npx tempolight --open` (Node.js 20+), or the one-file app, Homebrew, winget, Scoop, Docker (`ghcr.io/d4rkgeek/tempolight`), the Raspberry Pi image or the Home Assistant add-on.

## Set it up for someone

- [Set up with Claude](https://tempolight.pages.dev/setup-with-claude.txt): a step-by-step prompt to install Tempolight, find the lights, pick how it hears music, set the room and play a test song, using the HTTP API.
